reviewedFrom: Concurrency invariants for a ledger: any interleaving of independent sessions must end in a state some serial order could produce, or refuse with an explicit retryable error; money is never written twice or half-written; a closed period's saved statements match its ledger; repair converges. Each contention runs on fresh data several times through the product's own services, whose RPCs execute in separate database sessions. Amounts are integer cents.

double-close.derivation: Two closes of the same period at once: exactly one succeeds, the other refuses; one recognition entry, one saved statement per type, the worked-example July ledger.

close-versus-late-bill.derivation: A July bill against July's close in three orderings. Before: the bill posts, so the close refuses (WIP was reviewed without it). During: the bill is projected while the close holds July frozen; the freeze refuses the operational posting and the close completes without it. After: the closed period refuses the posting. Whenever July is closed, nothing operational lands in it afterwards and its saved balance sheet equals the ledger; repair (reopen, re-review, close) converges to both bills in July.

bank-double-match.derivation: One 500 bank debit matched to two different 500 checks at once, and two 500 bank debits matched to the same check at once: each time exactly one match is confirmed and no transaction or book line is over-matched.

deposit-receipt-contention.derivation: One 1,000 receipt claimed by two 1,000 bank deposits at once: one deposit posts, the other refuses; cash 1,000, undeposited funds 0.

concurrent-projection-runs.derivation: Three projection runs at once over the same five new bills: each bill posts exactly once.

proposal-double-approval.derivation: The same reviewed journal proposal approved twice at once posts one entry.

late-mutation-before-receipt.derivation: An independent session re-codes a bill after its journal is written but before the posting receipt is saved. The bill must not read 'posted' on the stale coding; the next run supersedes it, leaving one reversed and one posted entry on the new cost code.

entity-pair.note: Intercompany entity pairs arrive with B14.3.
